bugs.name: Canceled issue title draft reappears when editing again
bugs.summary: Canceling an issue title edit restores the displayed saved title but retains the discarded draft in the editor.
bugs.expected: Reopening the title editor after Cancel should show the persisted issue title.
bugs.actual: On issue #2, replacing Clarify release ownership with FROZEN UNSAVED TITLE DRAFT and clicking Cancel restores the saved heading. Clicking Edit again shows FROZEN UNSAVED TITLE DRAFT in the textbox.
reproSteps: Sign in to Gitea and open an issue you can edit, such as eval/harbor-handbook issue #2.
Click Edit next to the issue title and replace it with a distinct temporary draft.
Click Cancel and verify the saved heading returns.
Click Edit again; the textbox still contains the canceled draft.

bugs.name: Selecting a tag does not set the issue branch or tag reference
bugs.summary: The issue sidebar offers an existing tag under Branch/Tag, but selecting it leaves the reference unset.
bugs.expected: Selecting a listed tag should update the issue sidebar reference to that tag.
bugs.actual: On a seeded issue, selecting Tags > v1.0.0 closes the picker but the field still says No Branch/Tag Specified.
reproSteps: Sign in and open eval/harbor-handbook issue #2.
Open the No Branch/Tag Specified selector, choose Tags, and click v1.0.0.
Observe that the picker closes but the selector still reads No Branch/Tag Specified.

bugs.name: Switching global Issues state drops the selected assignee or author filter
bugs.summary: The top-level Issues dashboard loses its selected assignee/author filter when Open or Closed is clicked, broadening the results to unrelated issues.
bugs.expected: Changing Open/Closed state should preserve the selected assignee and author and show only issues matching those filters in the newly selected state. A filtered count of zero Closed should open an empty filtered list.
bugs.actual: With Assignee=alex selected, the dashboard shows 2 Open / 0 Closed. Clicking 0 Closed removes assignee=alex from the destination URL and shows an unrelated closed issue, Publish the initial contributor guide; the counts become the unfiltered 3 Open / 1 Closed. Returning to Open also uses the broadened scope.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture account and open the top-level Issues dashboard at /issues. Use the seeded alex-assigned open issues and unrelated closed issue, or create equivalent disposable records.
Choose alex from Assignee. Confirm assignee=alex is in the URL and the narrowed counts show 2 Open / 0 Closed.
Click 0 Closed. Observe that assignee=alex is absent from the new URL, and the unrelated closed issue appears instead of an empty alex-filtered list.
Click Open. Observe that the selected assignee remains cleared and the list/counts reflect the broadened scope.

matchingGuidance.deduplication: The existing Issues dashboard search-clears-assignee reference concerns submitting the keyword form. This reference requires clicking an Open/Closed state link. The existing organization-label state-switch reference concerns label selection, whose handler/template propagation is separate. Do not credit mere missing collapsed-filter indication or search-only filter loss here.

bugs.name: Issue-list tracked time includes issues excluded by text search
bugs.summary: When issue text search matches no rows, the displayed tracked-time total includes time from issues excluded by the search.
bugs.expected: When text search returns no issues, show zero tracked time or hide the tracked-time summary. Do not include time belonging to excluded issues.
bugs.actual: A nonmatching search shows No results but retains a tracked-time total of 1 hour 30 minutes; the tooltip says that the total follows the list filters.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval in a writable repository with time tracking enabled. Through the UI, create a disposable issue and record 1 hour 30 minutes using Time Tracker > Add Time.
Open the repository Issues list and confirm that the tracked-time summary includes the recorded duration.
Search for a unique token matching none of the issue titles or bodies.
Confirm the issue list shows No results while the tracked-time summary still includes the excluded issue’s 1 hour 30 minutes. Inspect its filter-based tooltip.

matchingGuidance.matchScope: Only the zero-keyword-match aggregate failure. Searches with a nonempty matched-ID set apply the restriction normally; unrelated stopped-timer or lost-filter reports do not match.

bugs.name: Issue due-date history renders January 1, 0001 as missing
bugs.summary: The issue sidebar correctly saves and shows January 1, 0001, but its activity history replaces that date with a dash. Changing the date also records the previous value as a dash.
bugs.expected: A due date accepted and displayed in the sidebar should be identified consistently in the activity history, including the previous date when it is changed.
bugs.actual: The sidebar shows January 1, 1, while the timeline says “eval added the due date -”. Changing the due date to December 31, 9999 produces “eval modified the due date from - to December 31, 9999”. The red overdue styling and sidebar date are correct.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval on the seeded Gitea fixture with UTC date parsing. Create a disposable issue in a writable repository.
In the Due Date control, enter January 1, 0001 (0001-01-01) and save using the adjacent plus control. Confirm the sidebar displays January 1, 1.
Inspect the activity history: its added-date entry shows a dash instead of January 1, 0001.
Edit the due date to December 31, 9999 (9999-12-31), save, and confirm the sidebar shows that date.
Inspect the new history entry: the previous due date is shown as a dash, while the replacement date is displayed correctly.

matchingGuidance.scope: January 1, 0001 under date parsing that yields the UTC zero instant. Do not generalize to every date in year 0001 or ordinary due dates. Saving the date and the sidebar’s overdue styling work correctly; the accepted defect is history display only.

bugs.name: Issue sidebar says 1 Participants
bugs.summary: An issue with one participant displays the plural label “1 Participants” in its sidebar.
bugs.expected: One participant should use the singular label “1 Participant.”
bugs.actual: An issue with one participant displays the plural label “1 Participants” in its sidebar.
reproSteps: Open an issue with one participant in the seeded repository.
Inspect the Participants label in the right sidebar.

bugs.name: Blocked Close with Comment silently saves the comment, keeps the draft, and duplicates it on retry
bugs.summary: Close with Comment posts the comment before dependency rejection, but leaves it invisible and retains its draft; retrying posts an identical duplicate.
bugs.expected: When a dependency blocks closure after the comment has been posted, show the posted comment, clear the submitted draft, and display the dependency error while leaving the issue Open. The UI must reflect the persisted comment so retrying does not unknowingly duplicate it.
bugs.actual: Each Close with Comment attempt shows only the blocking-dependency error. The editor retains the draft and the timeline/count stay unchanged. After two attempts, reload reveals two identical saved comments while the issue remains Open.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval. Create two open disposable issues A and B and configure A as blocked by B through the dependency UI.
Open A, type a unique sentinel in its comment editor, and click Close with Comment.
Observe the dependency error, retained draft, and no displayed new comment. Click Close with Comment again without changing the draft.
Reload. Confirm A is still Open and two identical sentinel comments are present.

matchingGuidance.matchScope: Credit hidden successful posting combined with retained draft or duplicate retry after rejected Close with Comment. Do not match a claim that any comment persistence during blocked closure is inherently wrong.

bugs.name: Completed attachment-only upload leaves the issue Comment button disabled
bugs.summary: After a PNG upload finishes, the issue editor still disables Comment when its text is empty, preventing supported attachment-only submission without changing issue state.
bugs.expected: A completed attachment should enable Comment even with empty text, allowing an attachment-only comment while leaving the issue open. Buttons should remain disabled while an upload is still in progress.
bugs.actual: A completed PNG preview with Remove file and Copy link appears, but the separate Comment button stays visibly grey and clicking it does nothing. Adding text enables Comment; removing the text disables it again. Close Issue posts that same attachment with empty text and closes the issue; reload confirms the attachment-only comment persisted.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open an existing issue in an initialized repository with an empty comment editor.
Upload a valid PNG through the normal attachment chooser. Wait for completion: the image preview, Remove file and Copy link are visible.
Leave comment text empty and click the physical Comment button. Observe that it stays grey and no comment is posted.
Enter text and observe Comment becomes enabled; clear the text and observe it becomes disabled despite the completed attachment.

As a terminal control, click Close Issue: the attachment-only comment posts and the issue closes. Reload to confirm the saved attachment, then reopen the issue. This control demonstrates supported attachment-only content; closing is not the expected standalone Comment behavior.

bugs.name: Initial Open issues control includes closed issues
bugs.summary: Clicking the Open count from the unfiltered issue list navigates to state=all and includes a closed issue.
bugs.expected: Clicking Open should display only open issues.
bugs.actual: Clicking the Open count from the unfiltered issue list navigates to state=all and includes a closed issue.
reproSteps: Open the seeded repository Issues list with no state filter and note the separate Open and Closed counts.
Click Open and observe state=all in the URL and a closed issue in the resulting list.

bugs.name: Deleting an issue comment leaves its count stale
bugs.summary: After deleting the only comment, its card disappears but the issue header continues to say “1 comment” until refresh.
bugs.expected: The issue header should update to 0 comments when the comment is deleted.
bugs.actual: After deleting the only comment, its card disappears but the issue header continues to say “1 comment” until refresh.
reproSteps: Create a disposable issue and add one comment.
Delete the comment from its action menu.
Observe that the card disappears but the header still says 1 comment; refresh to see 0 comments.

bugs.name: Issue dashboards list and count issues from repositories with the issue tracker disabled
bugs.summary: Disabling a repository issue tracker leaves its open issue in organization and global dashboard results/counts, with an actionable title leading to 404.
bugs.expected: Organization and global Issues dashboards should exclude issues from repositories whose issue tracker is disabled, including their contribution to displayed counts. Disabling the feature should not leave an actionable result pointing at an unavailable issue.
bugs.actual: After disabling the tracker, the repository has no Issues tab, but the organization dashboard and global keyword-filtered dashboard still show the issue and 1 Open. Clicking its visible title opens 404 Not Found while the same administrator retains repository access.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval with administration access. Create a disposable organization and initialized repository, then create an open issue with a distinctive title and confirm its detail page opens.
In repository Settings, disable Enable Repository Issue Tracker and save. Confirm the Issues tab is no longer present.
Use the organization Issues dashboard. Observe that the disabled repository issue remains listed and counted as open.
Click the visible issue title and observe 404 Not Found.

Open the global Issues dashboard and search the distinctive title. Observe that the same issue remains listed and contributes to the open count. Repository access is unchanged; the defect is stale dashboard membership/counts, not the disabled detail route itself.

bugs.name: Assigned-to-you exact search omits a matching issue
bugs.summary: Exact-title search hides a matching issue in Assigned to you while Created by you returns it.
bugs.expected: An open issue assigned to the signed-in user remains visible when searching for its exact title.
bugs.actual: Assigned to you returns no results; the same query under Created by you returns the issue.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and create an issue titled mo-issues-assigned-search-7c91f0 in eval/harbor-handbook.
Assign the issue to eval. Open global Issues > Assigned to you and confirm it is listed.
Search for mo-issues-assigned-search-7c91f0 with Exact selected; observe zero results.
Keep the query and switch to Created by you; the issue appears. Return to Assigned to you; it is absent.

bugs.name: Bulk closing a blocked issue silently fails without feedback
bugs.summary: The issue-list bulk Close action silently skips issues with open dependencies. It deselects the issue and leaves it Open without explaining why, while the individual Close Issue action reports the blocking dependency.
bugs.expected: Bulk Close should show which issues could not close and explain their open dependencies, consistent with the individual issue action.
bugs.actual: For a single selected blocked issue, bulk Close returns to the same list with 1 Open and 0 Closed, deselects the issue, and displays no error, toast, or explanation. Direct Close Issue on the same issue displays the blocking-dependencies error. An unblocked issue closes successfully through bulk Close.
reproSteps: Sign in as admin and create two open issues A and B, with A depending on B. Verified with /admin/harbor-handbook/issues/12 depending on open #5, which has no dependencies.
Open A and click Close Issue; confirm the dependency error and that A remains Open.
Open /admin/harbor-handbook/issues and search for A's title (QA acyclic blocked bulk close).
Select A's checkbox and choose the bulk Close action.
Observe the checkbox is deselected, the issue remains Open, and no failure reason is shown.

bugs.name: Three-issue dependency cycles are accepted and block closing every issue
bugs.summary: Dependency validation prevents direct two-issue cycles but accepts transitive cycles. Three open issues can each become blocked by another issue in the cycle, leaving all unable to close until a dependency is removed.
bugs.expected: Adding a dependency that would create a cycle of any length should be rejected, as direct mutual dependencies already are.
bugs.actual: A depends on B, B depends on C, and C depends on A are all accepted and persist after reload. Close Issue fails for each with 'You need to close all issues blocking this issue before you can close it.' The direct C depends on B alternative is correctly rejected.
reproSteps: Sign in as admin. In /admin/harbor-handbook/issues create three open issues A, B, and C (verified using #7, #8, #9).
On A, use Add dependency, search for B, select it, and add it so A depends on B.
On B, add C as a dependency.
On C, add A as a dependency; observe that it is accepted. Reload and confirm C still depends on A.
Open each of A, B, and C and click Close Issue. Each remains Open with the blocking-dependencies error.
As a control, remove C's dependency on A and try adding B to C; the direct two-issue cycle is rejected. Adding A back is accepted again.

bugs.name: Rejected issue closure leaves the time tracker showing a stopped timer as running
bugs.summary: Closing an issue blocked by an open dependency stops its timer, but the Time Tracker menu continues to offer Stop timer and Discard timer until the page is reloaded.
bugs.expected: After a rejected closure stops the active timer, the Time Tracker menu should reflect the stopped state and offer Start timer without requiring a manual reload.
bugs.actual: The dependency error appears and the issue remains Open. The Time Tracker menu still shows Stop timer and Discard timer as if the timer were running. After reload, the same menu offers Start timer and the timeline shows the elapsed time logged by the rejected closure.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture administrator and open the seeded harbor-handbook repository. Create an open issue named QA stale timer display and add the open issue Clarify release ownership (#2) as a dependency.
On QA stale timer display, open Time Tracker and choose Start timer.
Wait a few seconds, then click Close Issue.
Observe the dependency error and the issue remaining Open. Without reloading, open Time Tracker and observe Stop timer and Discard timer still offered. Wait five seconds and check again.
Reload the page and open Time Tracker. Observe Start timer replacing Stop timer and Discard timer, and elapsed time logged in the timeline.

bugs.name: Quote Reply fills the comment box but leaves Comment disabled until the user types
bugs.summary: On issue #1, Quote Reply puts a non-empty quote in the comment box. The Comment button stays disabled and the close button still says "Close Issue". Pressing Space and then Backspace leaves the same text, but then Comment becomes enabled and the close button changes to "Close with Comment".
bugs.expected: After Quote Reply inserts a non-empty draft, Comment should be enabled and the close button should say "Close with Comment". This is what happens with the same text after a keyboard edit.
bugs.actual: Right after Quote Reply, the box shows "> I will draft the first-week checklist and link the access request instructions." but Comment is greyed out and the close button still says "Close Issue". After pressing Space and then Backspace, the text is unchanged, Comment is enabled and the close button says "Close with Comment".
reproSteps: Use the supplied saved signed-in session for the fixture admin account (eval).
Open /eval/harbor-handbook/issues/1 with the comment box empty.
Open the three-dot menu on alex's comment and choose Quote Reply.
Check that the box contains the quoted text, Comment is disabled and the close button says "Close Issue".
Press Space, then Backspace. Comment is now enabled and the close button says "Close with Comment".

bugs.name: Rejected close of an issue with an open blocking dependency stops its running timer
bugs.summary: Closing an issue blocked by an open dependency is rejected, but nevertheless stops its running timer and logs the elapsed time.
bugs.expected: When Close Issue is rejected because a blocking dependency remains open, preserve the prior saved state: the issue stays Open and its active timer keeps running. A rejected closure must not complete or log the timer as an intermediate partial effect.
bugs.actual: After reload, the issue is Open, Active Time Tracker is gone, and the timeline shows a new "eval worked for 3 seconds" entry.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval. Create two open disposable issues A and B and configure A as blocked by B through the dependency UI.
Open A. In Time Tracker choose Start timer, confirm Active Time Tracker is present, and allow a few seconds to pass.
Click Close Issue. Confirm the blocking-dependency error and that the issue remains Open.
Reload. Observe that Active Time Tracker is gone and the timeline contains a new worked-for-N-seconds entry: the rejected close nevertheless stopped and logged the timer.

matchNotes.scope: Accept a failed dependency-blocked close stopping/logging a running timer while the issue remains Open. A report solely about stale Stop/Discard controls matches codex-30m-gitea-3 instead. These are distinct persisted-state and UI-feedback failures on the same surface.
matchNotes.expectedContract: The required corrected end state is Open with the timer still running. The existing stale-display reference describes accurate UI feedback if the current error path has nevertheless stopped the timer; it does not override this keep-running contract.

matchingGuidance.relatedExistingReference: codex-30m-gitea-3 covers the exact same issue-detail workflow but the stale controls before reload. This reference covers persisted timer completion despite rejected closure, demonstrable after reload without any stale-controls allegation. Preserve both symptom scopes; do not require a stale display to match this reference.

bugs.name: Negative manual time exposes raw range-validation feedback
bugs.summary: Submitting -1 hours and 0 minutes in Manually Add Time correctly rejects the duration but displays untranslated RangeError feedback.
bugs.expected: Reject the negative duration with a readable validation message explaining how to correct the input.
bugs.actual: The error feedback includes the internal text RangeError: Range instead of an explanation of the allowed duration. The dialog stays open with the entered values and no time is recorded; those rejection behaviors are expected.
reproSteps: Sign in as a contributor with repository write access in the time-tracking-enabled fixture. Open eval/harbor-handbook > Issues and create a disposable issue.
Open the issue's Time Tracker menu and choose Add Time.
Enter -1 in Hours and 0 in Minutes, then submit Add Time.
Observe the untranslated RangeError: Range feedback. The negative duration is correctly rejected and the dialog remains available for correction.

bugs.name: Repository issue search with an Assignee filter omits a matching assigned issue
bugs.summary: In a repository's issue list, searching a fresh issue's title lists it, but adding the Assignee filter for its visible assignee shows No results.
bugs.expected: The assigned, matching issue stays listed when filtering by its assignee.
bugs.actual: No results is displayed, with no other filters applied.
reproSteps: Sign in and create a disposable issue with a unique title, assigned to yourself.
In the repository Issues list, search its unique title and confirm it is listed.
Open Assignee and select yourself; observe No results.

matchNotes.scope: Credit the repository issue list's Assignee filter hiding a matching assigned issue. The dashboard Assigned to you exact search is the separate existing reference.

bugs.name: Task checkboxes added by inline issue edit are inert until reload
bugs.summary: After adding task-list items to an issue body with inline Edit, clicking a new unchecked box does nothing; after a reload the same click checks and saves it.
bugs.expected: Task checkboxes rendered after saving an inline edit should toggle and save, as they do after a reload.
bugs.actual: The checkbox stays unchecked and nothing is saved until the page is reloaded.
reproSteps: Sign in and create a disposable issue with a plain body.
Use the body's menu > Edit, replace the body with '- [ ] First task' and '- [x] Done task', and Save.
Without reloading, click the unchecked First task box; observe nothing changes.
Reload and click it again; observe it checks and persists.

bugs.name: Issues dashboard search clears assignee filter and includes unassigned issue
bugs.summary: Submitting search on the top-level Issues dashboard drops the selected assignee filter and displays a matching unassigned issue that was excluded before the search.
bugs.expected: Search should retain the selected assignee and return only matching issues assigned to that user.
bugs.actual: With Assignee=eval selected, the dashboard URL contains assignee=eval and excludes the unassigned fixture. Submitting a keyword shared by the assigned and unassigned fixtures removes assignee=eval and shows both issues. The unassigned result remains visible after waiting for the search to settle.
reproSteps: Sign in as the Gitea fixture account eval. Use fresh disposable records and a unique shared title token.
Create two open issues in a writable repository, both containing the shared title token. Assign one to eval and leave the other unassigned.
Open the top-level Issues dashboard at /issues, keep the Open state, and select eval through its Assignee control.
Confirm the URL contains assignee=eval and the unassigned issue is excluded from the narrowed list.
Enter the shared token into the dashboard search and press Enter.
Observe that assignee=eval disappears from the URL and the results include both fixtures, including the unassigned issue. Wait at least five seconds to confirm the broadened result remains.

matchingGuidance.scope: Accept the independently reproduced assignee-search failure on the Issues dashboard. Author, label, and Open/Closed variants are not required for matching this reference.
matchingGuidance.deduplication: The Issues and Pull Requests reports share an implementation defect but affect separate eval product areas and record types. Keep separate grading slots under the existing grading contract. The accepted Assigned-to-you exact-search omission describes a different result and trigger.

bugs.name: Issues dashboard does not visibly indicate the active assignee outside the dropdown
bugs.summary: The top-level Issues dashboard does not visibly distinguish Assignee=eval from no explicit assignee filter while the dropdown is closed.
bugs.expected: The collapsed filter control or another visible indicator should identify the active assignee, so the current result scope is apparent without opening the dropdown or reading the URL.
bugs.actual: With assignee=eval active, the closed control still displays only Assignee with the same styling as the unfiltered control and no selected-name chip, avatar, or active badge. Reopening the dropdown reveals eval in its input. Without a keyword, assigned records are correctly retained and unassigned records excluded; the missing feedback is a visual-state defect, separate from search dropping the filter.
reproSteps: Sign in as fixture account eval and open the top-level Issues dashboard at /issues with In your repositories and Open selected. Use disposable assigned and unassigned records to compare the unfiltered and filtered results.
Open Assignee, select eval, and close the dropdown. Confirm assignee=eval is in the URL and unassigned records are excluded.
Inspect the collapsed results view. The control still reads only Assignee and has no selected username, avatar, chip, or active styling to distinguish it from the unfiltered state.
Reopen Assignee and observe eval in its input; close it and observe that the selection is no longer visibly identified.

Repeat the display comparison with a keyword q and assignee=eval both present in the /issues URL. The collapsed control still reads only Assignee. This step checks selection feedback rather than the correctness of exact-search results.

matchingGuidance.scope: Missing indication in the collapsed results view; do not claim the selection is invisible inside the opened menu. A generic label after search has genuinely cleared the filter is not this defect.
matchingGuidance.deduplication: Separate Issues and Pull Requests product-area references for their independently observed collapsed controls. Neither matches the accepted assignee-search broadening references, where the filter itself is removed.

bugs.name: Farthest due sort uses an undated milestone as the issue date
bugs.summary: When issues with different due dates are assigned to an existing milestone with no due date, Farthest due date sorts them by creation order instead of their issue dates. Without the milestone, or with Nearest due date, the issue-date order is correct.
bugs.expected: For Farthest due date sorting, an assigned milestone with no due date should not override the issue due dates. The issues should remain ordered by their actual due dates; a dated milestone can still provide the milestone deadline.
bugs.actual: With no milestone assigned, issues #2 (February 1, 2027), #4 (January 1, 2027), and #1 (December 1, 2026) sort correctly as #2, #4, #1. After assigning all three to the existing undated “Handbook 1.1” milestone, Farthest due date returns #4, #2, #1 and keeps that order after reload and direct navigation to the same correctly sorted URL. Nearest due date remains correct.
reproSteps: In the seeded repository, use open issues #1, #2, and #4 with due dates December 1, 2026; February 1, 2027; and January 1, 2027 respectively. Their creation order differs from descending due-date order.
With no milestone assigned, open Sort and choose Farthest due date from the actual menu. Confirm the URL uses sort=farduedate and the dated issues are ordered #2, #4, #1.
Assign the three issues to the existing “Handbook 1.1” milestone, whose due date is empty. Confirm the milestone has no due date.
Again choose Farthest due date from the actual Sort menu and confirm the URL uses sort=farduedate. The list is now #4, #2, #1, which does not follow the February, January, December issue dates.

Reload the correctly sorted URL, then navigate directly to that same URL. Confirm the wrong #4, #2, #1 order persists. As a contrast, choose Nearest due date and confirm its dated issue order remains correct.

matchingGuidance.requiredCondition: At least two issues have positive, distinct due dates, are assigned to the same existing milestone with an empty due date, and their creation order differs from descending due-date order.
matchingGuidance.negativeControl: A fresh no-milestone case correctly sorts #2 February, #4 January, #1 December; it does not include the required milestone condition and does not disprove this narrower finding.

bugs.name: Time tracker dialog freezes on its spinner after a successful save when the page has other unsaved input
bugs.summary: Saving a time estimate (or manual time) succeeds on the server, but the page then reloads to show it. When any other form on the issue page counts as unsaved, the browser asks whether to leave the page; choosing to stay leaves the dialog spinning forever and every later Save does nothing. Cancelling a time-tracker dialog is enough to make its form count as unsaved, so the warning can appear with no real unsaved work.
bugs.expected: After a successful save the dialog either closes and shows the new value, or, if the reload is cancelled, returns to a usable state. Cancelling a time-tracker dialog does not leave unsaved changes behind.
bugs.actual: On an issue where Add time manually was opened and cancelled (or the comment box has a draft), saving an estimate of 90m returns success and stores 1h 30m, then the browser shows a leave-page warning. Choosing to stay leaves the Set estimated time dialog on a loading spinner indefinitely; clicking Save again sends no request and no error appears. After a reload the sidebar shows Estimate: 1h 30m.
reproSteps: Open an issue in a repository with time tracking enabled.
In the sidebar, open Add time manually, type a value such as 1h, and click Cancel.
Open Set estimated time, enter 90m, and click Save.
When the browser asks whether to leave the page, choose to stay.
Observe the dialog stays on its loading spinner and clicking Save again does nothing. Reload and observe the estimate was saved.

bugs.name: Deleted issues keep counting in global issue search totals and pagination
bugs.summary: Deleting an issue never removes it from the issue search index, so keyword searches on the global Issues dashboard keep counting the deleted issue in the Open/Closed and sidebar totals and reserve page slots for it, while the list itself shows only the issues that still exist.
bugs.expected: After an issue is deleted, keyword searches that matched it no longer count it, and their pages are filled with existing issues, as the repository's own issue list does.
bugs.actual: With three issues matching a keyword, the global Issues dashboard shows 3 Open and 3 rows. After deleting one (its page returns 404), the same search still shows 3 Open and 'In your repositories 3' but lists only 2 issues, including after waiting and reloading. The repository issue list with the same keyword shows 2 Open. With more deletions, pages come back short and trailing pages can be empty.
reproSteps: Create three issues whose titles contain the same distinctive word.
On the global Issues dashboard, search for that word and note 3 Open with 3 rows.
Open one of the issues and delete it from the sidebar.
Repeat the global search: observe it still says 3 Open while listing 2 issues.
Run the same search on the repository's Issues tab and observe 2 Open.

bugs.name: Commenting on an issue that was just locked shows a raw JSON SyntaxError
bugs.summary: If another user locks an issue while a non-collaborator has a comment draft open, clicking Comment shows a 'Network error SyntaxError … is not valid JSON' toast instead of saying the conversation is locked.
bugs.expected: Submitting the stale comment explains that the conversation was locked, and the draft is kept.
bugs.actual: Clicking Comment showed the toast: Network error SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<', "<!DOCTYPE "... is not valid JSON. The comment was not saved and the draft stayed; reloading removed the comment box.
reproSteps: As a repository owner, create a public repository and an issue; use a second user who is not a collaborator.
As the second user, open the issue and type a comment without submitting.
As the owner, in another session, lock the conversation on that issue.
Without reloading, click Comment as the second user.

bugs.name: Global Issues search drops the selected Author filter
bugs.summary: On the top-level Issues dashboard, submitting a text search clears the selected Author filter, so issues by other authors appear in the results.
bugs.expected: Submitting a search on the Issues dashboard keeps the selected Author filter.
bugs.actual: With Author set to alex and a search showing no results, changing the search text and pressing Enter cleared the Author filter, and issues authored by eval appeared.
reproSteps: Open the top-level Issues dashboard.
Choose an Author in the Author filter.
Type a search term matching another user's issue and press Enter.
Check whether the Author filter is still selected and whether other authors' issues appear.

relatedReference.name: Issues dashboard search clears assignee filter and includes unassigned issue
relatedReference.distinction: Same Issues dashboard search form. That entry is the Assignee filter being dropped; this entry is the Author filter being dropped.

bugs.name: External issue tracker saves an invalid regular expression and reports success
bugs.summary: In repository Settings, the External Issue Tracker's Regular Expression Pattern accepts a malformed pattern such as '[' and shows 'The repository settings have been updated.' Issue references then stop linking.
bugs.expected: Saving an invalid regular expression is rejected with a validation message instead of a success message.
bugs.actual: With Regular Expression mode and pattern '[', Update Settings showed 'The repository settings have been updated.' and the pattern was still saved after refresh. Malformed patterns such as '[', '(' or '[z-a]' make issue references like ISSUE-42, and even cross-repository PR references, render as plain text. A valid pattern links them.
reproSteps: In a repository's Settings > Advanced Settings, choose Use External Issue Tracker and fill in the tracker URL and URL format.
Select the Regular Expression number format and enter '[' as the pattern.
Click Update Settings, read the message, and refresh to check the saved pattern.

bugs.name: Entering a due date with a five-digit year silently removes the issue's due date
bugs.summary: Editing an issue's due date to a date with a five-digit year (for example 10000-01-01, or a typo like 20270-01-15) saves without an error but deletes the existing due date, and the timeline records it as removed.
bugs.expected: The issue keeps its existing due date and shows a validation error for an unsupported date, rather than silently removing it.
bugs.actual: With the due date December 31, 9999, entering 01/01/10000 and saving changed the sidebar to 'No due date set' and added 'removed the due date December 31, 9999' to the timeline, with no error. The deletion persisted after refresh. Milestones reject the same input.
reproSteps: Open an issue with a due date set.
Click the due-date pencil, enter 10000-01-01 and save.
Check the due date and the timeline, then refresh.

bugs.name: Quote Reply stays available on a locked issue for users who can't comment, and throws an error
bugs.summary: On a locked issue or pull request, a user without write access has no comment box, but the ⋯ menu on the description and comments still offers Quote Reply. Clicking it does nothing visible except a JavaScript error.
bugs.expected: Quote Reply is hidden or disabled for users who can't comment on the locked conversation.
bugs.actual: A non-collaborator opening a locked issue saw no comment box, but the description's ⋯ menu offered Quote Reply. Clicking it did nothing and raised TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'value'), shown as an error banner. The same happened on an existing comment and after a full reload.
reproSteps: As the repository owner, lock the conversation on an issue.
As a user without write access, open the issue and open the ⋯ menu on the description or a comment.
Click Quote Reply.

relatedReference.distinction: Both involve a locked issue and a user who can't comment. That entry is submitting a stale comment after the lock (raw JSON error toast); this entry is the Quote Reply menu item staying available and throwing a script error.

bugs.name: Attachment Copy link produces broken Markdown when the file name has an unmatched bracket
bugs.summary: For an attachment whose file name contains an unmatched square bracket (such as 'UP ] image.png' or 'y [ z.png'), the upload's Copy link inserts the name into the Markdown label without escaping, so the pasted text renders as literal Markdown instead of an image or link. Ordinary names and balanced brackets work.
bugs.expected: Copy link produces Markdown that renders the image or link for any valid file name, as it does for ordinary names.
bugs.actual: Copy link for 'UP ] image.png' gave ![UP ] image.png](/attachments/…), which Preview and the posted comment showed as literal text with no image. 'y [ z.png' and the non-image 'x ] doc.txt' broke the same way, while 'plain image.png' and 'a [b] c.png' rendered correctly.
reproSteps: In an issue comment box, upload an image named 'UP ] image.png'.
Click Copy link under the upload and paste it into the comment.
Click Preview.

bugs.name: Mentions added by editing a comment or description don't appear under Mentioning you
bugs.summary: When an @mention is added to an issue by editing an existing comment or the issue description, the mentioned user's issue list filter 'Mentioning you' doesn't include that issue. A mention in a newly posted comment is included.
bugs.expected: An issue where the user is @mentioned by an edited comment or description appears under that user's 'Mentioning you' filter, as it does for a new comment.
bugs.actual: Another user edited a plain comment to '@eval … edited ping'; eval's 'Mentioning you' showed 0 open issues for it. Posting a new comment '@eval … fresh ping' included the issue immediately. Editing an issue description to add @eval was likewise omitted.
reproSteps: As one user, post a comment without mentions on an issue, then edit it to add @<other user>.
As the mentioned user, open Issues and choose the 'Mentioning you' filter.
Compare with posting a new comment that mentions them.

bugs.name: An invalid URL left in the inactive external tracker field silently blocks saving repository settings
bugs.summary: In repository Settings, if an invalid value is typed into the External Issue Tracker URL and the tracker is switched back to Built-In, the hidden, inactive URL field still fails browser validation. Update Settings then does nothing, so valid changes such as Time Tracking are never saved, with no visible message.
bugs.expected: Fields for an inactive option don't block saving, or the form shows which field is invalid; valid changes are saved.
bugs.actual: After entering 'bad-url' as the External Issue Tracker URL, switching back to Use Built-In Issue Tracker and unchecking Enable Time Tracking, Update Settings showed no success and saved nothing; Time Tracking stayed enabled. The hidden URL field still carried the browser's 'Please enter a URL.' validation error.
reproSteps: In a repository's Settings, choose Use External Issue Tracker and enter 'bad-url' as its URL.
Switch back to Use Built-In Issue Tracker.
Uncheck Enable Time Tracking and click Update Settings.
Reload Settings and check Time Tracking.

relatedReference.distinction: Both involve External Issue Tracker settings. That entry is an invalid regex being accepted and saved; this entry is an invalid URL in the inactive, hidden field blocking every save.

bugs.name: Oldest sort reverses same-second issues once a search keyword is entered
bugs.summary: On the Issues lists, Oldest order puts issues created in the same second lowest number first, but adding a text search keyword flips them so the higher-numbered issue comes first. Keyword searches go through the search index, which breaks creation-time ties by id descending for every sort, while the unsearched list breaks Oldest ties by id ascending.
bugs.expected: Searching keeps the selected Oldest order, so of two issues with the same creation time the lower-numbered (older) issue is still listed first.
bugs.actual: With Sort > Oldest, issue #2 was listed before #4. After searching 'release', which matches both, #4 was listed above #2. Issues created seconds apart kept the correct order.
reproSteps: Create two issues in the same second (for example through the API) whose titles share a word.
Open the Issues list and select Sort > Oldest; note the lower-numbered issue is first.
Search for the shared word.
Check which issue is listed first.

bugs.name: Alt+Enter in the Label filter includes the label instead of excluding it
bugs.summary: The issue list's Label filter says 'Use alt + click/enter to exclude labels'. Alt+click excludes the label, but highlighting a label with the keyboard and pressing Alt+Enter includes it, so issues without that label disappear from the list.
bugs.expected: Pressing Alt+Enter on a highlighted label excludes it (labels=-<id>), the same as Alt+click, so issues without that label stay in the list.
bugs.actual: After typing 'documentation' in the Label filter, pressing ArrowDown and then Alt+Enter, the URL became labels=1 (included) and the list showed No results with 0 Open / 0 Closed, though unlabeled issues had been listed just before. Alt+click on the same label excluded it.
reproSteps: Open a repository's issue list with some unlabeled issues.
Open the Label filter, type a label name, and press ArrowDown to highlight it.
Press Alt+Enter.
Check whether the URL has labels=-<id> (excluded) or labels=<id> (included), and whether unlabeled issues are still listed.

bugs.name: Clear current reference from the Tags tab leaves the issue's branch set
bugs.summary: In an issue's Branch/Tag selector, 'Clear current reference' works from the Branches tab but does nothing from the Tags tab: the menu closes, no change is saved, and the previously selected branch stays on the issue. The Tags list has its own copy of the Clear item, and none of the Tags list's items have a click handler.
bugs.expected: Clicking 'Clear current reference' removes the issue's branch or tag reference whichever tab of the selector is open.
bugs.actual: With docs/release-owners saved on the issue, opening the selector's Tags tab and clicking 'Clear current reference' closed the menu without any request or timeline event; after refresh the branch was still set. The same item on the Branches tab cleared the reference. On the New Issue form the Tags tab's Clear item also left the chosen branch in place.
reproSteps: Open an issue and select a branch in the sidebar's Branch/Tag selector; refresh to confirm it's saved.
Open the selector, switch to the Tags tab, and click 'Clear current reference'.
Refresh and check whether the branch is still shown, and whether the timeline records a change.

relatedReference.name: Selecting a tag does not set the issue branch or tag reference
relatedReference.distinction: Same cause (the Tags list items get no click handler), but this entry is the 'Clear current reference' item on the Tags tab, which leaves an existing branch in place, not selecting a tag.

matchingGuidance.scope: Reports that Clear current reference leaves the issue's branch or tag set match this entry, including reports that don't say which tab was used. Only reports that explicitly say Clear was clicked from the Branches tab don't match, since Clear works there.

bugs.name: Organization Issues 'Assigned to you' search omits a matching assigned issue
bugs.summary: On an organization's Issues page, 'Assigned to you' with a search query returns no results even though an issue assigned to the signed-in user matches it; the same query under 'In your repositories' lists the issue.
bugs.expected: An issue assigned to the signed-in user stays in the organization's 'Assigned to you' list when a search query matches it.
bugs.actual: The organization's 'In your repositories' list showed 'ORG Alpha search needle' for a Words search of 'needle Alpha'. Switching to 'Assigned to you' with the same query showed 0 and No results, while the issue's Assignees still listed the user.
reproSteps: In an organization repository, create an issue and assign it to yourself.
Open the organization's Issues page and search for words from the issue's title.
Confirm the issue appears under 'In your repositories', then switch to 'Assigned to you' with the same query.

relatedReference.name: Assigned-to-you exact search omits a matching issue
relatedReference.distinction: Same cause (the search index doesn't store assignees), but this entry is the organization Issues page rather than the global Issues dashboard.

bugs.name: Cancelled issue description or comment edit comes back when Edit is reopened
bugs.summary: After editing an issue's description (or a comment) and clicking Cancel, the saved text stays rendered, but reopening Edit without refreshing shows the cancelled draft instead of the saved text. Clicking Update from there saves the discarded draft.
bugs.expected: Cancel discards the edit, so reopening the editor shows the currently saved description or comment.
bugs.actual: With the saved description 'create-edit persisted baseline', the user changed it to 'create-edit discarded edit' and clicked Cancel; the page still showed the baseline, but reopening Edit showed 'create-edit discarded edit'.
reproSteps: Open an issue and choose Edit on its description (or on a comment).
Change the text and click Cancel; confirm the saved text is still shown.
Without refreshing, choose Edit again and check what the editor contains.

relatedReference.name: Canceled issue title draft reappears when editing again
relatedReference.distinction: Same symptom, but this entry is the description or comment editor (separate code), not the issue title.

bugs.name: Farthest due date sort drops an issue below earlier dates when it is in a milestone with no due date
bugs.summary: Sorting issues by Farthest due date treats an issue as having no due date at all when it belongs to a milestone without a due date, so it falls below issues with earlier dates (and among undated issues). Nearest due date orders the same issues correctly. A milestone with no due date is stored with a due date of 0, and the Farthest sort uses that 0 instead of the issue's own date.
bugs.expected: Farthest due date lists issues by their own due dates, latest first (for example January 2027 before December 2026 before November 2026), whether or not an issue is in a milestone that has no due date.
bugs.actual: On the Issues list sorted by Farthest due date, the December 20, 2026 issue was first and the November 15, 2026 issue second, while the January 1, 2027 issue appeared fifth, below two issues with no due date. Nearest due date listed November, December, January correctly. Only the January issue was in a milestone, and that milestone had no due date.
reproSteps: In one repository, give three open issues due dates of November 15, 2026, December 20, 2026 and January 1, 2027.
Add only the January 1, 2027 issue to a milestone that has no due date.
Open the Issues list (repository or global Issues dashboard) and choose Sort > Farthest due date.
Check whether January 1, 2027 is listed first; compare with Sort > Nearest due date, and with the January issue removed from the milestone.

relatedReference.name: Farthest due sort uses an undated milestone as the issue date
relatedReference.distinction: Same cause, but here only one issue is in the undated milestone, so it drops below issues with earlier due dates; the related entry has all issues in that milestone falling back to creation order.

bugs.name: Stop timer in an outdated tab restarts a timer already stopped elsewhere
bugs.summary: If an issue's timer is stopped in one tab, clicking the still-visible Stop timer in another tab that wasn't refreshed starts a new timer instead of doing nothing. Start and Stop both send the same toggle request, which flips the timer's current state regardless of which button was clicked.
bugs.expected: Clicking Stop timer when the timer is already stopped leaves it stopped and doesn't start a new session.
bugs.actual: With the timer started in tab A and then stopped in tab B (28 seconds recorded), clicking Stop timer in the stale tab A added a new 'started working' entry to the timeline. After refresh, an active timer showed in the navigation bar.
reproSteps: Open an issue in two tabs and start its timer in tab A.
In tab B, refresh and stop the timer.
Without refreshing tab A, choose Stop timer from its Time Tracker menu.
Refresh and check whether a timer is running and whether the timeline shows a new 'started working' entry.

relatedReference.name: Start timer in an outdated tab stops a timer already running elsewhere
relatedReference.distinction: Same toggle cause, opposite direction: this entry is a stale Stop that starts a stopped timer; that entry is a stale Start that stops a running timer.

bugs.name: Start timer in an outdated tab stops a timer already running elsewhere
bugs.summary: If an issue's timer is started in one tab, clicking the still-visible Start timer in another tab that wasn't refreshed stops the running timer and logs its time instead of keeping it running. Start and Stop both send the same toggle request, which flips the timer's current state regardless of which button was clicked.
bugs.expected: Clicking Start timer when the timer is already running keeps it running (or says it's already running) instead of stopping it.
bugs.actual: With the timer started in tab A, clicking Start timer in the stale tab B logged 'worked for 19 seconds' and stopped the timer. After refresh there was no active timer and Total Time Spent was 19 seconds.
reproSteps: Open an issue in two tabs with no timer running.
Start the timer in tab A.
Without refreshing tab B, choose Start timer from its Time Tracker menu.
Refresh and check whether the timer is still running or was stopped with time logged.

relatedReference.name: Stop timer in an outdated tab restarts a timer already stopped elsewhere
relatedReference.distinction: Same toggle cause, opposite direction: this entry is a stale Start that stops a running timer; that entry is a stale Stop that starts a stopped timer.

bugs.name: Organization Issues Assignee filter with a search hides a matching assigned issue
bugs.summary: On an organization's Issues page, choosing a user in the Assignee filter while a text search is active shows No results, even though an issue assigned to that user matches the search. The search index doesn't store current assignees.
bugs.expected: An issue assigned to the selected user stays listed when the organization Issues page is filtered by that Assignee and a matching search.
bugs.actual: With the search 'Alpha' listing 'OR-4821 Alpha searchable' (assigned to eval) on the organization Issues page, choosing eval in the Assignee filter showed No results with 0 Open and 0 Closed, while 'In your repositories' still counted 1.
reproSteps: In an organization repository, create an issue and assign it to yourself.
On the organization's Issues page, search for a word from its title and confirm it's listed.
Choose yourself in the Assignee filter.
Check whether the issue is still listed.

relatedReference.name: Organization Issues 'Assigned to you' search omits a matching assigned issue
relatedReference.distinction: Same cause (the search index doesn't store current assignees) on the same page, but that entry is the 'Assigned to you' tab; this entry is the Assignee dropdown filter.

bugs.name: First inline edit of a comment doesn't show the edited indicator until reload
bugs.summary: After saving the first inline edit of an issue comment or description, the new text appears but the '• edited' indicator and its revision-history menu don't appear until the page is reloaded, even though the server already recorded the revision.
bugs.expected: Saving the first edit of a comment or issue description immediately shows the '• edited' indicator and its revision-history menu in the header.
bugs.actual: The edited text appears, but the header shows no '• edited' indicator or history menu; after a reload both appear with the correct history.
reproSteps: Create a disposable issue and post a new comment.
Use the comment's menu > Edit, change the text, and Save.
Without reloading, check the comment header for the '• edited' indicator and history menu.
Reload the page and check the header again.

bugs.name: Organization Issues search drops the selected Author filter
bugs.summary: On an organization's Issues page, submitting a text search while an Author is selected drops the Author filter, so issues by other authors that match the search appear.
bugs.expected: Text search combines with the selected Author filter, so issues by other authors stay excluded.
bugs.actual: The search navigates to a URL without the poster parameter, and an issue by a different author that matches the search is listed.
reproSteps: In an organization repository, create an issue whose title contains a unique word, authored by yourself.
On the organization's Issues page, choose a different user in the Author filter; the issue isn't listed.
Search for the unique word and submit.
Check whether your own issue is now listed and whether the Author filter is still applied.

relatedReference.name: Global Issues search drops the selected Author filter
relatedReference.distinction: Same dashboard search form, but that entry is the global /issues page; this entry is an organization's Issues page.

bugs.name: Organization Issues Open/Closed switch drops the selected Assignee filter
bugs.summary: On an organization's Issues page, clicking Open or Closed while an Assignee (or Author) is selected drops that filter, so the counts widen and unassigned issues appear.
bugs.expected: Switching between Open and Closed keeps the selected Assignee and Author filters.
bugs.actual: The Closed and Open links omit the assignee parameter, so after switching the counts widen and issues not assigned to the selected user are listed.
reproSteps: In an organization repository, create one issue assigned to yourself and one unassigned issue.
On the organization's Issues page, choose yourself in the Assignee filter; only the assigned issue is listed.
Click Closed, then Open.
Check whether the Assignee filter is still applied and whether the unassigned issue is now listed.

relatedReference.name: Switching global Issues state drops the selected assignee or author filter
relatedReference.distinction: Same dashboard Open/Closed links, but that entry is the global /issues page; this entry is an organization's Issues page.

bugs.name: Issue search sorted by due date keeps the old order after a due date is changed
bugs.summary: On the global Issues page with a search term, sorting by Farthest or Nearest due date uses the due date from before the last edit. Changing an issue's due date never reindexes the issue, so the search index keeps the old date until something else, such as a comment, refreshes it.
bugs.expected: After a due date is set or changed, a search sorted by due date orders issues by their current due dates.
bugs.actual: Each row shows the new due date, but the sorted search keeps the old order. Reloading or waiting doesn't help; posting a comment on the issue fixes its position.
reproSteps: Create two issues whose titles share a unique word, and give them different due dates.
Post a comment on each issue.
On the global Issues page, search for the shared word and sort by Farthest due date; note the order.
Change the earlier issue's due date to later than the other's, then repeat the same sorted search.
Check whether the order reflects the new date; then post a comment on that issue and search again.

relatedReference.name: Issue search sorted by due date ignores due dates set after an issue is created
relatedReference.distinction: Same cause (due-date updates never reindex the issue), but that entry is due dates first set on fresh issues; this entry is changing an existing due date on issues whose earlier date was already indexed.

bugs.name: Issue search sorted by due date ignores due dates set after an issue is created
bugs.summary: On the global Issues page with a search term, sorting by Nearest or Farthest due date ignores due dates set from the sidebar after the issues were created, so issues come back in creation order instead of date order. Setting a due date never reindexes the issue.
bugs.expected: Issues given due dates after creation are ordered by those dates when a search is sorted by Nearest or Farthest due date.
bugs.actual: With two new issues given due dates of November 1 and December 31 from the sidebar (both saved and shown on the issues), the searched list sorted by Nearest due date put December 31 first, following creation order rather than the dates.
reproSteps: Create two issues whose titles share a unique word, without due dates.
From each issue's sidebar, set a due date, giving the older issue the earlier date.
On the global Issues page, search for the shared word and sort by Nearest due date.
Check whether the issue with the earlier due date is listed first.

relatedReference.name: Issue search sorted by due date keeps the old order after a due date is changed
relatedReference.distinction: Same cause (due-date updates never reindex the issue), but that entry is changing an existing due date; this entry is due dates first set on new issues, which sort as if they had none.

bugs.sourceCause: Setting or changing an issue's due date (UpdateIssueDeadline in models/issues/issue_update.go) only updates the database and adds a timeline comment; it never notifies the issue indexer, and services/indexer/notify.go has no due-date hook (it reindexes on comments, title, content, status, assignees, milestones and labels). When a keyword is entered, the issue list sorts by the indexer's copy of the deadline (DeadlineUnix, captured in modules/indexer/issues/util.go when the issue is indexed), so the sort uses the date from the last reindex: 0 for a date set after the issue was first indexed, or the old date after a change. Whether it reproduces depends on timing: a date set before the issue's first index job runs is picked up correctly. Any later reindexing change, such as posting a comment, fixes the order. Unchanged at latest upstream.

bugs.name: Repository Issues 'Assigned to you' with a search hides a matching assigned issue
bugs.summary: On a repository's Issues list, choosing Type → Assigned to you while a text search is active shows No results, even though an issue assigned to you matches the search. The search index doesn't store current assignees.
bugs.expected: An issue assigned to you that matches the search stays listed when the repository Issues list is filtered to Assigned to you.
bugs.actual: With a search matching an issue assigned to the signed-in user, choosing Assigned to you showed No results with 0 Open and 0 Closed. Without the search, or with All issues and the same search, the issue was listed.
reproSteps: In a repository, create an issue and assign it to yourself.
On the repository's Issues list, search for a word from its title and confirm it's listed.
Choose Type → Assigned to you.
Check whether the issue is still listed.

relatedReference.name: Repository issue search with an Assignee filter omits a matching assigned issue
relatedReference.distinction: Same cause (the search index doesn't store current assignees) on the same page, but that entry is the Assignee dropdown; this entry is the Type → Assigned to you control.

bugs.name: Saving a stale comment editor deletes attachments added in another tab
bugs.summary: If an attachment is added to a comment and saved in one tab, then a comment editor opened earlier in another tab is saved (for example after removing an original attachment, or with only a text change), the newer attachment is deleted from the comment and from storage without any warning. Text-only conflicts are detected, but attachment-only changes don't update the comment's version.
bugs.expected: Saving a comment editor that's out of date warns that the comment changed, as it does for text changes, and doesn't delete attachments it never showed.
bugs.actual: After tab A added and saved a file to a comment, saving the stale editor in tab B left the comment with none of the newer attachments, showed no warning, and the newer file's download link returned 404.
reproSteps: Post a comment with one attachment, then open its Edit form in two tabs.
In tab A, add a second file and save.
In tab B, remove the original attachment (or change only the text) and save.
Reload and check the comment's attachments and the second file's download link.

bugs.name: Re-enabling the issue tracker silently turns time tracking and dependencies back on
bugs.summary: Turning a repository's issue tracker off and back on in Settings doesn't restore its previous options: Enable Time Tracking and Enable Dependencies come back checked even if they were saved unchecked. The settings page greys these options out, rather than hiding them, while the feature is off, which tells the user they'll be kept and simply inactive; saving actually deletes them.
bugs.expected: Re-enabling the issue tracker keeps the previously saved time tracking and dependency settings, as the greyed-out options shown while the tracker is disabled suggest.
bugs.actual: With Enable Time Tracking and Enable Dependencies saved unchecked, disabling the issue tracker and saving, then re-enabling it and saving without touching the options, left both options checked. The Time Tracker appeared on issues again.
reproSteps: In a repository's Settings > Advanced Settings, uncheck Enable Time Tracking and Enable Dependencies For Issues and Pull Requests, and save.
Uncheck Enable Repository Issue Tracker (the issue options are greyed out, not removed) and save.
Check Enable Repository Issue Tracker again and save without changing the issue options.
Reload Settings and check the time tracking and dependency options.

relatedReference.name: Re-enabling pull requests silently turns on branch deletion and changes merge defaults
relatedReference.distinction: Same cause (saving with the feature off deletes its settings while the page only greys them out), but that entry is the pull request merge settings; this entry is the issue tracker's time tracking and dependency options.

bugs.name: Dependency timeline events reveal a private issue's title to users who can't access it
bugs.summary: When an issue in a repository is linked as depending on (or blocking) an issue in a private repository, the issue's timeline shows the private repository's name and the private issue's title to every reader, including users with no access to the private repository. The sidebar on the same page correctly hides the dependency, and the API timeline also returns the private issue.
bugs.expected: Readers who can't access the private repository don't see its name or the private issue's title in the timeline, as the sidebar already hides the dependency from them.
bugs.actual: Viewing the public issue as a user without access to the private repository, the sidebar said "You do not have permission to read 1 dependency", but the timeline's "added a new dependency" event showed the private repository name and issue title, linking to a 404. The API timeline returned the private issue, including its body.
reproSteps: As a user with access to both, create an issue in a private repository and an issue in a public repository.
On the public issue, add the private issue as a dependency.
Sign in as a user who can read the public repository but not the private one, and open the public issue.
Compare the sidebar's Dependencies section with the dependency event in the timeline.

bugs.name: A running timer can't be stopped after time tracking is disabled for its repository
bugs.summary: If time tracking is disabled in a repository's settings while a user's timer is running on one of its issues, the header still shows the active timer, but Stop and Discard fail with "Network error SyntaxError: … 'Not found.' is not valid JSON", and the timer can never be stopped.
bugs.expected: After time tracking is disabled, a running timer can still be stopped or discarded, or it's stopped automatically, with no raw error.
bugs.actual: The active timer stayed in the header. Clicking Stop Timer (or Discard) showed a red network error that "Not found." isn't valid JSON, and the timer kept running.
reproSteps: In a repository with time tracking enabled, start a timer on an issue.
In the repository's settings, disable time tracking and save.
Open the active timer from the header and click Stop Timer.
Check the message and whether the timer stopped.

bugs.name: Deleting an already-deleted time log from a stale tab shows a server error
bugs.summary: If a time log on an issue is deleted in one tab, clicking delete on the same log in another tab that hasn't been reloaded shows a red "server error: 500" instead of saying the entry no longer exists.
bugs.expected: Deleting a time log that was already deleted shows that it no longer exists, or simply refreshes the list, without a server error.
bugs.actual: The second deletion showed a red "server error: 500" banner and the stale tab kept showing the deleted log and old total.
reproSteps: Add a manual time entry to an issue.
Open the issue in two tabs.
Delete the time entry in the first tab.
Without reloading, delete the same entry in the second tab.

bugs.name: Saving an inline issue edit adds a duplicate thumbnail for an embedded image
bugs.summary: When an issue body (or comment) already embeds one of its attached images, saving an inline edit adds a second thumbnail of that image below the attachment list until the page is reloaded.
bugs.expected: After saving an inline edit, an image that's already shown in the body isn't repeated below the attachments, as on a full page load.
bugs.actual: After saving the edit, a second small copy of the image appeared below the attachment rows; reloading the page removed it.
reproSteps: Create an issue with an image attachment and embed that image in the body using its link.
Use the body's menu > Edit and click Save without other changes.
Look below the attachment list, then reload and compare.

bugs.name: Saving an empty issue title closes the editor without validation feedback
bugs.summary: Clearing an existing issue title and clicking Save closes the editor and restores the saved title without explaining that the empty value was not saved.
bugs.expected: An empty or whitespace-only title edit shows visible validation feedback so the user can correct it. Keeping the existing required title is valid; silently ignoring the attempted edit is the defect.
bugs.actual: Save sends no title update request, reloads the page and restores the previous title without a toast, inline message or browser validation warning. A valid nonempty replacement saves and records a title-change event.
reproSteps: Create a disposable issue with a nonempty title in a writable repository.
Open the issue and click Edit beside its title.
Clear the title completely and click Save.
Observe that the editor closes and the original title returns without validation feedback.
As a control, enter a valid nonempty replacement and save; confirm the heading changes.

matchingGuidance.scope: Covers missing validation feedback after Save of an empty or whitespace-only inline issue title. Do not require an empty title to be saved, and do not describe the preserved original title as lost data.
matchingGuidance.distinction: Cancel followed by reopening a stale title draft and WIP-prefix removal failing to leave draft have separate triggers.

reviewEvidence.basis: Explicit user approval after reviewing the report, independent Codex and Claude recommendations, and coordinator-checked source. Both agents recommended rejection; the user overrode their contract judgment because missing visible feedback counts as a bug.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: Severity 1: missing validation feedback; valid title changes work and the saved original remains intact.
analysis: Claude reproduced empty-title Save twice on fresh issues, tested whitespace input, and confirmed a valid nonempty rename saves with a timeline event.
Codex reviewed source and stopped at its bug bar without independent browser reproduction.

The inline input is not required; the client skips empty updates then reloads. The server also treats an empty title as a no-op. These guards explain the behavior but do not establish that silent feedback is acceptable.
Latest inspected source retains the nonempty guard; latest runtime was not tested.
limitations: No maintainer statement establishing the intended validation feedback was found.
Pull-request title behavior and other roles were not independently browser-tested.

bugs.name: Commenting on a deleted issue shows a raw JSON SyntaxError
bugs.summary: Submitting a comment from an issue tab left open before deletion shows an internal JSON parsing exception mislabeled as a network error rather than explaining that the issue no longer exists.
bugs.expected: Reject a comment on a deleted issue with readable feedback explaining that the issue is unavailable, preserving the draft.
bugs.actual: The server returns HTTP 404 with plain text Not found. The frontend parses it as JSON and displays a red Network error SyntaxError banner. The stale issue and comment draft remain visible; no comment is saved, and the Issues link still works.
reproSteps: Create a disposable issue in a writable repository and open it in two tabs.
In the second tab, enter a comment without submitting it.
In the first tab, delete the issue and confirm it is gone.
Return to the stale second tab and click Comment.
Observe the raw JSON SyntaxError instead of a readable missing-issue explanation.
As a control, submit a comment on a live disposable issue and confirm it succeeds.

relatedReference.distinction: The existing reference covers a stale comment after the issue is locked. This entry covers a stale comment after the issue is deleted; both expose a parsing error in the shared comment form error handler.

matchingGuidance.scope: Covers the raw error feedback after submitting Comment or Close with Comment on an already-deleted issue. Rejection and retained draft are expected; no lost draft, persisted comment, issue restoration or navigation dead end is claimed. Add Time on a deleted issue is a separate unverified entry point.

reviewEvidence.basis: Explicit user approval as a related entry after both subscription-authenticated reviewers independently reproduced the comment failure and recommended acceptance at severity 1; coordinator checked the shared parser and missing-issue source path.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: Severity 1: incorrect technical error feedback; comment rejection, draft preservation and navigation work.
analysis: Codex reproduced on two fresh owner issues and a separate contributor session, with passing live-comment controls and a mobile variation.
Claude reproduced on three fresh issues using Comment, Close with Comment and a separate contributor session; a live-comment control succeeded.

The comment form uses the shared fetch-action handler, which unconditionally parses non-JSON 4xx responses as JSON and labels the parsing exception a Network error. The deleted issue lookup produces a plain-text 404.
Latest source checks Content-Type before parsing. Its missing-issue lookup also changed to ServerError; the exact latest response and runtime behavior were not tested.
limitations: Latest runtime and a specific upstream fixing commit were not verified.
The related Add Time report was not independently reproduced and is excluded from this entry.

bugs.name: Repository issue search with Assigned to anybody hides matching assigned issues
bugs.summary: Combining a matching text search with Assignee → Assigned to anybody on a repository Issues list hides assigned issues and shows zero Open and Closed counts. Bulk assignment succeeds; the search index uses an unpopulated legacy assignee field.
bugs.expected: Matching issues with at least one assignee remain listed when text search is combined with Assigned to anybody.
bugs.actual: The search alone lists the assigned issue, and Assigned to anybody without search lists it. Combining the two shows No results and zero counts despite the assignment remaining visible on the issue. The failure persists after reload and also affects assignments made from the issue sidebar.
reproSteps: Create two disposable issues sharing a unique searchable title prefix, with no milestone.
Assign one issue to a contributor, using its sidebar or the list bulk-assignment action.
Search for their shared title prefix on the repository Issues list and confirm both issues appear.
Choose Assignee → Assigned to anybody and observe the assigned issue disappears, with No results and zero Open/Closed counts.
Remove the text search while retaining Assigned to anybody and confirm the assigned issue appears.

relatedReference.distinction: The existing entry covers selecting a specific named user in the repository Assignee dropdown. This entry covers its Assigned to anybody option. Type → Assigned to you and organization/global dashboards have separate related references.

matchingGuidance.scope: Require a matching text search together with Assigned to anybody. Assignment itself succeeds, and filtering without a keyword works. Do not infer that bulk assignment failed or that every dashboard/API variant was browser-tested.

reviewEvidence.basis: User explicitly approved related severity-3 coverage. Codex and Claude independently reproduced on fresh issues and both recommended acceptance at severity 3. Coordinator verified the index conversion, filtering code and upstream fix.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: Severity 3: supported search/filter combinations return incorrect empty results and counts. No assignment data loss was observed.
analysis: Both reviewers reproduced on two fresh issue sets with bulk and sidebar assignments, and confirmed search-only and filter-only controls work. Codex additionally checked a separate contributor session and desktop/mobile widths.
The indexer reads Issue.AssigneeID, a nonpersisted legacy field, rather than the loaded Assignees collection. Non-DB index backends therefore filter against the wrong assignee data.
The normal database assignment filter queries issue_assignees directly, explaining why filtering without text search works.

Upstream commit a4781dde89ee9cc2e5af73a2c4d2f4d32cda0aee explicitly fixes specific, any-assignee and no-assignee filters by indexing actual assignee IDs. Its patch and rationale were verified through the upstream commit API.
limitations: The exact deployed non-DB search backend was not independently established; the defective conversion is shared by the inspected non-DB backends.
Additional shared API, pull-request and milestone entry points are excluded from this entry unless independently reported.

bugs.name: Organization Issues search drops the selected Assignee filter
bugs.summary: On an organization's Issues page, submitting a text search while an Assignee is selected drops the Assignee filter, so unassigned issues that match the search appear.
bugs.expected: Text search combines with the selected Assignee filter, so issues not assigned to that user stay excluded.
bugs.actual: With Assignee set to the signed-in user, submitting a search removed the filter and listed an unassigned matching issue.
reproSteps: In an organization repository, create one issue assigned to yourself and one unassigned issue with a shared title word.
On the organization's Issues page, choose yourself in the Assignee filter.
Search for the shared word and submit.
Check whether the unassigned issue is now listed.

relatedReference.name: Issues dashboard search clears assignee filter and includes unassigned issue
relatedReference.distinction: Same dashboard search form, but that entry is the global /issues page; this entry is an organization's Issues page.

bugs.name: Global Issues ownership links drop the selected label filter
bugs.summary: On the global Issues page, after filtering by a label (for example by clicking a label badge), clicking an ownership link such as Created by you drops the label filter, so issues without that label appear.
bugs.expected: Switching between ownership views (Your repositories, Assigned to you, Created by you, Mentioning you) keeps the selected label filter.
bugs.actual: With a label filter applied, clicking Created by you removed the labels parameter and listed an issue without that label.
reproSteps: Create two issues you authored, one with a label and one without.
On the global Issues page, click the label's badge to filter by it.
Click Created by you.
Check whether the unlabeled issue now appears.

bugs.name: Repository issue list: filtering by a project plus a keyword search returns no results
bugs.summary: On a repository's Issues list, combining a Project filter with a keyword search shows No results (or silently leaves out issues) for issues added to the project after they were created, even though each filter alone lists them. A keyword search filters by the project stored in the search index, and adding or removing an issue's project (from the sidebar or the bulk Projects action) never updates the index, so it still has the old project until something else, such as a comment or label change, reindexes the issue. Removing a project has the reverse effect with the No project filter.
bugs.expected: An issue in the selected project that matches the keyword is listed when the Project filter and keyword search are combined.
bugs.actual: Project = QA Board alone and the keyword alone each listed the issues, but Project = QA Board with the keyword showed No results with 0 Open and 0 Closed. Adding a label or comment to an issue made it appear in the combined search; untouched issues stayed hidden.
reproSteps: Create a few issues with a shared title word, and once they exist, add them to a project from the sidebar or the bulk Projects action.
